decision.justification: Two independent views of this merchant disagree with its declaration. The storefront presents a different business, and the infrastructure channel agrees. Neither could have produced the other: a merchant cannot change its payment behaviour without changing its actual business, and cannot change its interface without changing what customers see.

narrative.text: Merchant MID100013 declared digital_services at onboarding 224 days ago. Telemetry agrees: the largest deviations from the digital_services baseline are velocity_drift at +12.0 sigma (observed 0.887 against a category baseline of 0.00222), chargeback_rate at +2.8 sigma (observed 0.0124 against a category baseline of 0.00454), round_share_recent at +2.3 sigma (observed 0.654 against a category baseline of 0.329). The checkout surface presents a crypto_exchange interface at 0.95 confidence, against a declared category of digital_services. This vertical cannot be approved on this platform. Linked to 6 other merchants by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle. Their payment behaviour is also moving in step (synchrony 0.81), which independent businesses do not do. It is linked to 6 other merchant accounts by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle, and those accounts are moving in step (synchrony 0.81). A verification call was placed and produced no usable statement, which counts neither for nor against the merchant. In total 2 independent views of this merchant contradict its declaration. The investigation used 4 of a permitted 8 steps and stopped because confidence threshold met. Recommended tier restricts settlements, corroborated by the infrastructure channel; the storefront alone would not have been sufficient.
